verdict.rationale: Unstructured's own docs describe a structured data extractor: you define your own target JSON schema, and it extracts values from source files into that shape as JSON records. It is reachable through the API or Python SDK via an extract-job quickstart. Nothing documents validating outputs against the schema (required fields, type enforcement, error reporting on non-conforming values), so only the core extraction half of the story is evidenced. missing for 10: documented schema validation/enforcement of extracted fields, supported JSON Schema feature details, independent or hands-on corroboration of extraction accuracy.

support.subject: As a developer, I supply a JSON schema and get back validated structured fields extracted from the document

citations.quote: Define your own target JSON schema and have Unstructured extract values from your source files and data records directly into that shape in JSON format.
Unstructured then extracts values in a consistent JSON format that matches your fields, ready to use in your own applications.
Create a job to extract only the data that you care about from your documents, which Unstructured outputs as JSON object data records in a format that you define.
Later, you'll extract structured fields from an example medical intake form.
